title: Real-time Vector Ingestion
summary: Keep retrieval synchronized with changing source systems using versioned events, idempotent processing, and measurable visibility lag.
overview: Real-time vector ingestion moves source changes into a searchable index with a defined freshness objective. It usually combines change data capture or application events with parsing, chunking, embedding, and index writes. Real-time is a latency target across this pipeline, not a guarantee that an acknowledged event is immediately visible to every query.

The difficult cases are ordering, duplicate delivery, deletes, permission changes, and reprocessing after a model upgrade. Stable document versions and idempotent writes prevent old events from replacing newer evidence. Tombstones and authorization updates deserve the same reliability as content additions because stale access can be more serious than missing search results.

production.poc: A prototype measures elapsed time from source commit to successful retrieval for a changed record.
production.production: Production adds durable offsets, deduplication, version checks, dead-letter handling, and explicit deletion propagation.
production.scale: Enterprise scale separates backfills from live updates, monitors partition lag, and supports index migrations without starving current changes.

components.name: Change capture source
components.role: Emits committed content, deletion, and permission changes with stable identity.

components.name: Durable event log
components.role: Buffers updates and preserves replay positions.

components.name: Transformation workers
components.role: Parse and chunk documents using a versioned policy.

components.name: Embedding and index writers
components.role: Create compatible vectors and apply idempotent versioned updates.

components.name: Freshness verifier
components.role: Checks when a committed source revision becomes searchable and old revisions disappear.

flow.title: Capture committed change
flow.description: Record source identity, revision, operation type, and ordering information.

flow.title: Validate and transform
flow.description: Check schema and access metadata before producing versioned chunks.

flow.title: Embed changed content
flow.description: Reuse unchanged chunk hashes and generate vectors only for required updates.

flow.title: Apply index mutation
flow.description: Upsert new revisions and remove superseded chunks with conditional ordering safeguards.

flow.title: Commit processing position
flow.description: Advance the durable offset only after the required index operation succeeds.

flow.title: Verify visibility
flow.description: Probe retrieval freshness and deletion propagation separately from write acknowledgment.

diagrams.title: Version-aware event application
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant L as Change log
 participant W as Index worker
 participant V as Vector store
 participant F as Freshness monitor
 L->>W: Document revision event
 W->>V: Read applied revision
 V-->>W: Current revision
 W->>W: Reject stale event or transform new revision
 W->>V: Apply idempotent upsert or tombstone
 V-->>W: Write acknowledgment
 W->>L: Commit processing position
 F->>V: Probe search visibility
diagrams.caption: Write acknowledgment and query visibility are separate milestones with separate monitoring.

useCase.title: Updating outage knowledge during restoration
useCase.situation: A network assistant answers internal questions using incident tickets and restoration notes.
useCase.problem: Batch indexing leaves resolved incidents appearing active and misses newly identified affected areas.
useCase.requirement: Make committed updates searchable within a defined freshness target and remove superseded status.
useCase.architecture: A change stream feeds version-aware chunking and embedding workers with a dedicated live-update queue.
runtime: An incident status changes and emits a new source revision.
The index writer replaces old chunks and a probe confirms that current status is retrievable.
useCase.failure: A delayed older event is rejected by revision comparison instead of reopening the incident in the index.
useCase.impact: Track source-to-search latency, deletion lag, and failed-event age; queue throughput alone does not prove current answers.

tradeoffs.cost: Add ordering, replay, and operational complexity.
Requires resource allocation and scheduling policies.

failures.detection: Offset progress stops on repeated transformation errors.
failures.recovery: Quarantine the record with evidence and continue according to the consistency contract.
Reconcile source inventory and replay durable tombstones.

mistakes.fix: Use source versions and conditional writes.

mistakes.mistake: Rebuilding all embeddings for every edit
mistakes.fix: Hash chunks and reuse unchanged representations.

whenToUse: Use for frequently changing operational knowledge.
Use when stale status causes incorrect agent actions.
Use when deletion and permission propagation have explicit objectives.
whenNotToUse: Avoid streaming complexity for rarely changed small corpora.
Do not promise instantaneous consistency without store support.
Avoid live pipelines without replayable event history.
